title: Status Cadence, Triage-to-Restoration Runbook and Responder Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
This page defines a single runbook that covers the full incident lifecycle from first signal through triage, containment, restoration, and customer-facing status cadence. It combines responder playbook rules, sample status messages, postmortem requirements, and a game-day syllabus so teams can practice end-to-end incident handling with consistent customer communications.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated, and Redwood Private control-plane incidents where customer-visible degradation (latency, errors, or availability) or data-plane anomalies occur.
- Excludes internal build failures that do not affect customer traffic (see eng-infra runbooks).

Key definitions
- P0: Total outage or sustained >50% customer requests failing for 5+ minutes.
- P1: Major degradation causing elevated errors/latency across multiple customers or routes for 10+ minutes.
- SLO breach: Any single route where 99th-percentile latency > 2x target or error rate > 5% over 10 minutes.

Roles & responsibilities
1) Incident Commander (IC) - owns coordination, stakeholder updates, and prioritization.
   - Primary: oncall-engineer for service owner.
   - Secondary: team lead or senior SRE if IC unavailable.
2) Lead Responder - technical triage and remediation (may be multiple).
3) Communications Owner - drafts status updates and customer-facing messages.
4) Postmortem Author - documents root cause, timeline, impact, and action items.
5) Oncall Backup - takes over after 2-hour shift or at IC request.

Incident lifecycle (high level)
1) Signal & Acknowledge
   - Alerts from Prometheus/Alertmanager, Observability Console, automated SLO-detector, or customer report.
   - IC acknowledges within 2 minutes for P0, 10 minutes for P1.
2) Initial Triage (0–10 minutes)
   - Verify scope and blast radius (routes, regions, customers).
   - Collect quick evidence: recent deploys, infra changes, autoscaler events, kernel OOMs, GPU failures.
   - Determine P-level and declare incident.
3) Containment (10–30 minutes)
   - Apply immediate mitigations: circuit-breaker, route remap, rollback, scale-up, static-capacity warmup.
   - Preserve forensic data (profiles, KV caches, coredumps) and tag logs.
4) Restoration (30–180 minutes)
   - Implement root fix or safe fallback. Validate with smoke tests and canary traffic.
5) Recovery & Close (>180 minutes)
   - Confirm stability for two consecutive 15-min windows, then move to closure.
6) Postmortem (within 72 hours)
   - Publish timeline, root cause, impact, corrective actions, and owners.

Triage checklist (quick reference)
- Is the issue global or region-specific?
- Which models/routes are impacted? (chat/generation/embeddings/rerank)
- Recent deploys or config changes in last 60 minutes?
- Error-class fingerprints (500s, 429s, timeout, model OOM).
- Resource signals: GPU mem err, node reboots, AZ network flaps.
- Is the Canary or Dedicated pool showing degraded metrics?

Escalation matrix
- P0: Notify IC -> Pager (all-hands for service) -> Exec on-call if >30 minutes unresolved.
- P1: Notify IC -> Pager -> Senior SRE on backup list if >60 minutes.
- If customer data exposure suspected: immediate Security/Privacy page and Legal notification (see security-and-compliance/audit-logging).

SLOs and thresholds (operational targets)
- API availability: 99.95% monthly. Critical route availability target: 99.9%.
- Error rate: <0.5% 5xx on aggregate; SLO trigger when route 5xx > 1% over 10 minutes.
- Latency: p95 < 150ms, p99 < 450ms. Alert when p99 > 2x target for 10 minutes.
- Customer impact window: track number of customers and percent of routed tokens affected.

Status cadence (customer-facing)
- Initial acknowledgement: within 15 minutes for P0/P1. Short single-sentence summary + next update ETA.
- Regular updates: every 30 minutes for P0 until stabilization, every 60 minutes for P1.
- Resolution notice: include root cause summary, restoration steps, and any mitigations for customers.
- Postmortem link: published within 72 hours with technical details and customer impact summary.

Customer status templates
- Initial (P0)
  Subject: Redwood status: Major service disruption affecting [service/region]
  Body: We are investigating elevated errors affecting [service/routes/region]. Customers may experience increased latency and request failures. Our oncall team is actively triaging. Next update: [ETA]. For urgent questions contact support@redwood.com with incident ID: [INC-ID].

- Update (mid-incident)
  Subject: Redwood status update: [short summary] — [INC-ID]
  Body: What changed: [brief note]. Current status: [mitigation in place / traffic partially restored / routing fallback active]. Impacted customers: [list or "broadly"]. Next update: [ETA].

- Resolution
  Subject: Redwood incident resolved: [service/region] — [INC-ID]
  Body: Summary: the incident that caused [symptoms] has been resolved at [time UTC]. Root cause: [concise root cause statement]. Customer impact: [affected routes/customers/time window]. Remediation and next steps: [rollout, hardening, follow-up]. Postmortem: [link].

Runbook snippets (common scenarios)
1) Model inference latency spike (generation APIs)\   - Verify whether problem is model-specific: check model variant metrics and KV cache hit-rate.\   - If a single model variant causing spike, shift traffic to verified fallback (model: redwood-lite-v1 -> redwood-stable-v1) and enable quantized profile.\   - If kernel-level GPU stalls detected: drain affected GPU, re-schedule workloads, and open a GPU-fleet ticket.\2) Backend datastore timeouts (config store or user metadata)\   - Check DB connection pools and read replicas.\   - Apply circuit-breaker at API layer, use cached responses for read-only endpoints.\   - Rollback recent schema migrations if correlated to deploy timestamp.\3) Region network degradation\   - Reroute traffic to healthy region per smart-routing policy.\   - Notify cloud provider and set support ticket.\   - If cross-region state sync affected: disable cross-region writes and operate read-only for affected region.

Forensic preservation steps
1) Preserve logs and tracing window: tag and extend retention for implicated hosts/services.
2) Snapshot KV cache and upload to incident storage with access logs.
3) If coredump created, store with obfuscated customer identifiers and notify Security.

On-call rotation & handoff guidance
- Rotation length: 7 days for primary oncall engineers. Secondary SRE rotates monthly.
- Handoff checklist (before leaving shift):
  - Confirm incident list and active mitigations.
  - Update bridge and status page.
  - Verify runbook references and open tickets assigned.
  - Confirm oncall backup acknowledged handoff.
- Incident fatigue policy: no engineer should serve more than two high-severity (P0/P1) incidents in a single rotation without cadence-adjusted break. Notify manager for relief.

Game day syllabus (quarterly)
- Objective: validate end-to-end triage, customer comms, and cross-team escalation for a region-level outage and a model regression scenario.
- Participants: service owners, SRE, Support, Product, Security representative.
- Exercises:\  1) Simulated region network partition at T0: validate routing failover and customer status cadence.\  2) Silent model quality regression at T30: detect via eval pipeline and trigger rollback + customer notice.
- Success criteria: mean time-to-detect < 10 minutes, mean time-to-restore < 45 minutes for simulated P1, customer comms delivered within 15 minutes.

Postmortem template & timeline
- Publishable within 72 hours. Required sections (publish to confluence page and link in status):\  - Title: concise summary and incident ID\  - Severity: P0/P1/P2\  - Timeline: minute-granular events from first signal to recovery\  - Impact: affected customers, % of requests, duration\  - Root cause analysis: technical cause + contributing factors\  - Corrective actions: short-term and long-term with owners and due dates\  - Detection & mitigation metrics: detection time, restore time, and verification plan\  - Follow-ups: verification tests and scheduled review (owner + date)

Post-incident follow-up cadence
- 24 hours: internal hotwash meeting to capture missing facts.
- 72 hours: publish postmortem draft and share with reviewers.\- 2 weeks: closure meeting for action items and verification of mitigations.

Instrumentation & telemetry requirements for incidents
- Mandatory signals to attach to incident: p95/p99 latency, 5xx error rate, request volume by route, model-KV cache hit-rate, GPU error counters, autoscaler events.\- Ensure all incidents are tagged with incident ID in log traces and alert annotations.

Document maintenance and ownership
- Owner: eng-sre team.
- Review cadence: annual review and after any P0.
- Game days: scheduled quarterly; rotation owners must run at least one per year.

Appendix: example internal incident status message (IC -> Execs)\- Subject: [INC-ID] P0 - Service degradation affecting Redwood API (summary)\- Body: Time: [T0 UTC] | Current status: partial traffic restored to 63% | Impact: 45% of customers saw errors on /v1/generate | Action taken: traffic staged to fallback model, GPU nodes drained in eu-west-1 | Next ETA: 30m | IC: @aisha.patel
